selection_rationale: This candidate directly addresses the core CNSM topic (operational reliability of LLM-driven NetOps) by empirically testing a formal-verifier-as-oracle inside a GVR loop. It is falsifiable, experimentally clear, feasible within the stated model-call budget, and maps to key unresolved gaps (integration of formal verification with GVR). Reviewer concerns are addressable via concrete preregistration repairs.
unresolved_uncertainties: Verifier coverage relative to vendor-specific CLI semantics and completeness of the verifier model (evidence gap U2).
Potential verifier/emulator semantic mismatch: verifier decisions (accept/reject) may not align with emulator (ground-truth) outcomes, producing false-accepts or false-rejects.
Risk that the repair loop will overfit to the verifier (satisfy verifier rules but fail under emulator dynamic/stateful semantics).
Emulator limitations (Mininet/Kathará) in representing real device dynamic/stateful behaviors (evidence gap U1).
Model/API rate limits, transient failures, or retry behavior biasing results if not strictly controlled.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Validate verifier coverage against a gold-labelled subset (human-reviewed or device-executed) and report verifier false-accept and false-reject rates.
Include conservative and permissive verifier rule-sets and preregister sensitivity analyses comparing them.
Provide anti-overfitting safeguards for the repair loop (e.g., diversity-promoting objectives, verifier+emulator checks) and log full repair transcripts for audit.
Predefine and freeze a retry policy and model-call budget; instrument and report API failures and their deterministic handling (retries vs. abort).
